subNodes.text: first of all, in web.js, the login page doesnt have CSRF protection. that's pretty huge - i can plant XSS in my own notes, and now that i dont need a token to log in, i can prob just POST /login with my credentials which will redirect me to /notes
if i get to /notes then my XSS will execute! but then what the hell do i do with that?

well, the problem with fetching /notes earlier was that we needed to request from the same origin in order to pass CORS policy. but now if my XSS is on the noted website itself, it's inherently the same origin and thus it can also fetch /new to create new posts, which is something i couldn't do earlier
ok, cool. so once again, what the hell do i do with that? great, i can make new notes on my own account! i could always do that though!
this is where claude absolutely clutched - apparently theres a couple tricks I can use with window.open
didn't know this but when you call window.open, it returns a reference to that window which you can store in a variable

yknow how we do document.querySelector, or like addEventListener("onload", ...)? well of course that's calling window.document.querySelector, and window.addEventListener. that window object at the front can be any window object though
if i do sth like var win = window.open("0.0.0.0:8080/notes"); as long as i'm still same-site i can pull a casual win1.document.querySelector("..."); because win1 is also a window object.
ok, but still, how does that help us? how does the XSS get access to the window that my JS URL is storing a reference to? apparently there's a way.
there's a lot more parameters in window.open (didn't know that either lol). one of those params is target - basically when you do a window.open call, you can name that specific call
e.g., I can do window.open("0.0.0.0:8080", "win1"); this new window is now called win1 in the browser memory
notice how i didnt store that as a variable. that's fine, because i can get a reference to that window with something like var win = window.open("", "win1");
even though we're not changing the location of that specific window object, the window.open call to that specific named target will still return a reference to that target. THIS IS THE SOLUTION.

that makes sense now. puppeteer in the goto method doesn't like javascript pseudo-urls. it DOES support data urls though, so we can make an html data url that already has the form pre-built and that has a <script> which submits it;
